title: Paranormal investigator in Newcastle to share family Amityville experience
excerpt: Chris McKinnell's two North East dates will include a Halloween special and a ghost hunt in Northumberland

Paranormal investigator in Newcastle to share family's experiences that inspired Amityville and Conjuring films

Chris McKinnell's two North East dates will include a Halloween special and a ghost hunt in Northumberland

13:36, 08 Oct 2026

The grandson of famous American paranormal investigators is bringing a chill to Newcastle this week as he shares his family legacy in a tour that includes two North East dates, with the second being in Northumberland on the night of Halloween itself. Chris McKinnell's grandparents, Ed and Lorraine Warren, established a ghost-hunting group in the US in the early 1950s and their decades of experiences included investigations which inspired the Amityville Horror and The Conjuring Universe films.

‌

‌

Their grandson will be discussing the cases behind those and other real-life investigations during a talk in the city this Friday night. Seven Stories, the national centre for children's books, might not seem a natural first choice for an evening of scary-sounding stories but it's there that McKinnell will be discussing his family's - and his own - investigations and delving into cases that many know about only through movies, also including the likes of Annabelle and The Nun.

‌

Seven Stories says that as a "venue built around stories, imagination and bringing extraordinary tales to life", it actually "provides a particularly fitting backdrop for an evening exploring the real stories behind some of the world's most famous paranormal cases". McKinnell grew up surrounded by them and went on to become an investigator in his own right, working alongside his grandparents and spending decades researching hauntings, unexplained phenomena and consciousness.

‌

He is now the director of the Warren Legacy Foundation for Paranormal Research. Audiences can expect to hear about investigations spanning decades, including those from the Warren archives as well as McKinnell's own, and he will discuss the separation between 'fact and fiction'.

They will have an opportunity to ask him questions towards the end of the talk - and there's an opportunity to meet him too, with VIP tickets being available for the event. A spokesperson said: "The event is less about Hollywood horror and more about hearing the stories directly from someone who was part of the family and the investigations themselves.

‌

"Chris will also take questions from the audience and discuss how his views on paranormal phenomena have developed over the years." Following his Newcastle stop, McKinnell's tour will also take him to Ashington on October 31, for a Halloween special in a much more apt-sounding venue: The Haunted Headquarters, which is a former 1800s police station and courthouse now turned paranormal investigation venue which is also set to open a crime and punishment museum.

Tickets for An Evening with Chris McKinnell cost £25 while the VIP option is £45 which includes - besides a pre-event meet-and-greet with the star of the show - priority seating and a signed copy of his book The Warren Legacy. The event at The Haunted Headquarters also has a VIP Plus ticket option, for £75, which will enable the audience to continue the evening with a ghost hunt through the venue with McKinnell in attendance.

For details of his tour see here and to book for the October 9 event at Seven Stories see here or for the October 31 at The Haunted Headquarters book here. Doors will open at 7pm each evening and the shows will start at 7.30pm.
